Title: Artificial intelligence in systematic reviews: opportunities and challenges
Authors: Marshall, I.J.; Wallace, B.C.
Abstract: We review the current state of AI tools for systematic review automation, covering screening, extraction, and synthesis. We identify key challenges including bias, reproducibility, and the need for human oversight.
Concepts: systematic review; artificial intelligence; machine learning; automation; bias

Title: Automating data extraction in systematic reviews: a systematic review
Authors: Jonnalagadda, S.R.; Goyal, P.; Huffman, M.D.
Abstract: This paper reviews methods for automated data extraction from full-text articles in systematic reviews, evaluating NLP and machine learning approaches.
Concepts: data extraction; NLP; systematic review; automation; machine learning

Title: Active learning for title and abstract screening in systematic reviews
Authors: van de Schoot, R.; de Bruin, J.; Schram, R.
Abstract: We present ASReview, an active learning tool for title and abstract screening. In simulation studies, it reduces the number of records screened by up to 95%.
Concepts: active learning; screening; systematic review; ASReview; machine learning

Title: ROBOT reviewer: extracting data from randomised controlled trial reports
Authors: Marshall, I.J.; Kuiper, J.; Wallace, B.C.
Abstract: ROBOT reviewer uses machine learning to extract data from RCT reports, including PICO elements and risk of bias assessments.
Concepts: RCT; data extraction; PICO; machine learning; risk of bias

Title: Semi-automated screening of biomedical citations for systematic reviews
Authors: Olorisade, B.K.; Brereton, P.; Andras, P.
Venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association
Abstract: We evaluate semi-automated screening tools for biomedical systematic reviews, finding that SVM-based approaches achieve recall above 95% with significant workload reduction.
Concepts: screening; SVM; biomedical; systematic review; recall

Title: A comparison of machine learning methods for screening in systematic reviews
Authors: Blaizot, A.; Veettil, S.K.; Saidoung, P.
Abstract: Comparing logistic regression, SVM, and neural networks for abstract screening, we find that simpler models perform comparably to deep learning with smaller training sets.
Concepts: machine learning; screening; logistic regression; SVM; neural networks

Title: Large language models for information extraction in systematic reviews
Authors: Guo, E.; Gupta, M.; Deng, J.
Abstract: We evaluate GPT-3 and similar LLMs for structured data extraction from clinical trial reports, finding high accuracy on PICO elements with appropriate prompting.
Concepts: LLM; GPT-3; information extraction; PICO; clinical trials

Title: Reporting standards for AI-assisted systematic reviews: a scoping review
Authors: Khalil, H.; Ameen, D.; Zarnegar, A.
Abstract: We identify 14 reporting standards relevant to AI-assisted systematic reviews and propose a checklist for transparent reporting of AI tool use.
Concepts: reporting standards; transparency; systematic review; AI; checklist

Title: Human-in-the-loop machine learning for systematic review screening
Authors: Cormack, G.V.; Grossman, M.R.
Abstract: We propose a continuous active learning framework for systematic review screening that maintains human oversight at each iteration, achieving high recall with minimal human effort.
Concepts: active learning; human-in-the-loop; screening; systematic review; recall

Title: Automated screening versus manual screening: a meta-analysis
Authors: O'Mara-Eves, A.; Thomas, J.; McNaught, J.
Abstract: Meta-analysis of 23 studies comparing automated and manual screening in systematic reviews. Automated tools achieve mean recall of 0.97 (95% CI 0.95–0.99) with 50% workload reduction.
Concepts: meta-analysis; automated screening; manual screening; recall; workload

Title: Bibliometric analysis of AI in systematic reviews: 2010–2022
Authors: Nakagawa, S.; Lagisz, M.; O'Brien, A.M.
Abstract: Bibliometric analysis of 1,247 publications on AI in systematic reviews reveals exponential growth since 2018, with active learning and NLP as dominant themes.
Concepts: bibliometrics; AI; systematic review; active learning; NLP

Title: Ten simple rules for using AI in systematic reviews
Authors: Syriani, E.; David, I.; Kumar, G.
Abstract: We present ten practical guidelines for researchers integrating AI tools into systematic review workflows, emphasising transparency, validation, and human oversight.
Concepts: guidelines; AI; systematic review; transparency; validation

Title: Zero-shot classification for systematic review screening using GPT-4
Authors: Alshami, A.; Elsayed, M.; Ali, E.
Abstract: We evaluate GPT-4 zero-shot classification for abstract screening across five systematic reviews, achieving recall above 0.96 without any training data.
Concepts: GPT-4; zero-shot; screening; systematic review; recall

Title: PRISMA 2020 and AI-assisted reviews: a methodological note
Authors: Rethlefsen, M.L.; Kirtley, S.; Waffenschmidt, S.
Abstract: We discuss how the PRISMA 2020 statement applies to AI-assisted systematic reviews and propose extensions to the flow diagram for AI-mediated screening steps.
Concepts: PRISMA 2020; AI; systematic review; reporting; flow diagram

Title: Open-source tools for AI-assisted literature screening: a comparative evaluation
Authors: Tsou, A.Y.; Treadwell, J.R.; Erinoff, E.
Abstract: We compare Rayyan, ASReview, Covidence, and DistillerSR on five systematic reviews, evaluating recall, precision, and usability for researchers without programming experience.
Concepts: Rayyan; ASReview; Covidence; screening; usability

Title: Automated PICO extraction using transformer models
Authors: Nye, B.; Li, J.J.; Patel, R.
Abstract: We fine-tune BERT and RoBERTa for PICO extraction from clinical trial abstracts, achieving F1 scores above 0.85 on all four PICO elements.
Concepts: PICO; BERT; transformer; extraction; clinical trials

Title: Reducing workload in systematic review updates using active learning
Authors: Cleo, G.; Scott, A.M.; Islam, F.
Abstract: Active learning reduces the screening workload for systematic review updates by 60–80% while maintaining recall above 0.95 in simulation studies.
Concepts: active learning; systematic review update; screening; recall; workload

Title: Hallucination in LLM-assisted systematic reviews: risks and mitigations
Authors: Sallam, M.
Abstract: We document hallucination rates in LLM-assisted data extraction and propose validation strategies including side-by-side auditing and structured output prompting.
Concepts: hallucination; LLM; systematic review; validation; auditing

Title: Ethical considerations in AI-assisted evidence synthesis
Authors: Booth, A.; Clarke, M.; Ghersi, D.
Abstract: We identify five ethical domains relevant to AI-assisted evidence synthesis: algorithmic bias, transparency, accountability, data privacy, and the role of human judgment.
Concepts: ethics; AI; evidence synthesis; bias; transparency

Title: Living systematic reviews and AI: a framework for continuous evidence synthesis
Authors: Elliott, J.H.; Synnot, A.; Turner, T.
Abstract: We propose a framework for living systematic reviews that integrates AI-assisted screening and extraction with human oversight, enabling continuous evidence updates.
Concepts: living systematic review; AI; continuous synthesis; human oversight; framework
